clue.text: Hard closures after reorganisation

indicators.note: once the word closures has been reorganised its letters stand in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about the tough shutdowns that followed a company restructure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reorganisation' rearranges the letters of CLOSURES. 'Hard' looks like it describes the closures, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sclerous is a medical and botanical term for hardened or bony tissue.

clue.text: Throat of rook involved in its cry

indicators.note: one piece is involved in, wrapped up inside, the other

parts.note: the cry of a rook or crow is a caw
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that the rook's throat is used in making its call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts R (rook in chess notation) inside CAW, the rook's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A craw is the crop of a bird, and loosely the throat or gullet of any animal.

clue.text: As time is out, clear the bar

indicators.note: something that is out is not in its proper order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder for the anagram, taken as written
to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: Closing time has come, so the landlord empties the pub of drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear the bar' reads as emptying a pub at closing time; 'the bar' is the definition, and 'is out' signals the jumble of the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe selling drinks, a kind of bar.

clue.text: Accelerate and start shooting

definitions.meaning: to speed up, as a driver putting the throttle open
to begin firing, as guns opening fire

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to give an engine more throttle and to begin firing guns.

clue.text: Take steps to implement Pro crustean measure

definitions.meaning: to go for a walk, literally taking steps
Procrustes of Greek myth stretched his guests to fit his bed, so his measure lengthens limbs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro crustean' is the newspaper's split of Procrustean; the myth's innkeeper racked short guests until they fitted his bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go for a walk, and taken literally it describes Procrustes lengthening a victim's limbs.

clue.text: State company importing one type of cloth

indicators.note: importing means bringing something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation of California, a US state
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A US state firm brings in a single kind of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' signals the container; 'State' is a cue for a US state abbreviation rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton fabric, so it is a variety of cloth.

clue.text: Bound to get better one, in part

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to land a better single part in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is a noun meaning a leap; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriole is a leap in classical horsemanship, a jump made from all four legs.

clue.text: Records entered controversially

definitions.meaning: written registers or tallies of items
to enter the ... is to join a contest or dispute, the ... being a jousting arena

explanation.definitionFit: Lists are written records; the lists were also tournament grounds, so entering them means joining a fight.

clue.text: In petty fashion, offering food in cold shelter

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, so the word for cold surrounds the other piece

parts.note: chilly means cold
a dish is a serving of food offered at table

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited host serves meagre food in a freezing hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelter' is the container signal: the cold word wraps round the food, so the answer breaks in the middle of its first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Childishly means in an immature, small-minded way, like a sulky infant.

clue.text: Put off one's stride, stall old banger

parts.note: to rattle someone is to unsettle them
the trap is the starting stall in greyhound racing

explanation.surface: Something throws a runner off balance and halts an ancient car.
explanation.walkthrough: An old banger is British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a rickety, rattling vehicle, exactly what a worn-out jalopy is.

clue.text: Leave out captain

definitions.meaning: the captain of a curling or bowls team

explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to omit; a skip, short for skipper, leads a team in bowls or curling.

clue.text: Face ace on base behind bars

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece sitting on another follows it

parts.note: a mount is the base or backing on which something is set
A is the card abbreviation for ace
someone behind bars is inside, in prison slang

explanation.surface: A climber confronts the top pilot sitting on the base, with prisoners nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' signals that the ace comes after the base in this across answer. 'Face' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountainside is the face or slope of a mountain, the steep side a climber tackles.

clue.text: Close decision

definitions.meaning: the end or finish of something

explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion is both the ending of something and a verdict arrived at by reasoning.

clue.text: Bellyache of chap who's hungry?

indicators.note: who's is read as who has, so the chap has something within him

parts.note: a man is a chap
a hungry belly holds nothing, and nothing is O

explanation.surface: A starving fellow grumbles about his stomach pains.
explanation.walkthrough: The hungry chap has nothing inside: O (zero) placed inside MAN. 'Bellyache' is a verb here meaning complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellyache is informal for to grumble or complain, just as a moan is a whinge.

clue.text: Stop eating and get a grip

annotationWithheld.why: Stop eating and get a grip: HOLD (stop) + FAST needs 'Stop' twice, as HOLD and inside 'Stop eating' for FAST; no parse found with each word doing one job
annotationWithheld.clue: Stop eating and get a grip

clue.text: Impertinent failures producing policy reversals

parts.note: flip means flippant or impertinent
flops are failures

explanation.surface: Cheeky blunders lead a government into U-turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn in policy is called a flip-flop, from the idea of turning over.

clue.text: Plunged in one foreign sea, with others going in

annotationWithheld.why: Plunged in one foreign sea, with others going in: I + MER gives part, but no reading of 'with others going in' supplies the remaining M, S, E, D; possibly garbled in OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: Plunged in one foreign sea, with others going in

clue.text: National paper that is distributed Mon-Sat

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means that is to say

indicators.note: letters distributed are scattered about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A paper with national reach is delivered every weekday and Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' signals the anagram. 'National' doubles as a citizen of Scotland, so the definition covers both the newspaper and the man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scotsman is an Edinburgh-based newspaper, and a Scotsman is a national of Scotland.

clue.text: Lounge is empty

definitions.meaning: without substance or purpose, as in vain threats

explanation.definitionFit: Idle means both to laze around and, of words or threats, hollow and meaningless.

clue.text: Before trouble mounted, owned up to bloomer

indicators.note: before places the following piece ahead of the trouble piece
in a down clue going up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: had means owned

indicators.note: something mounted climbs upward, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a howler before things got worse.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'mounted' and 'up' both signal reversals; 'Before' orders the pieces. 'bloomer' means a flower, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden flower, and a bloomer is something that blooms.

clue.text: Digs by Welsh river, finding old weapon

parts.note: digs, British slang for lodgings, are quarters
the Taff is the river through Cardiff

explanation.surface: Someone lodging beside a river in Wales turns up an ancient arm.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarterstaff is a long wooden pole used as a weapon in medieval England.

clue.text: Dissolute male with redhead, one preparing the bed?

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: A debauched man and a ginger companion head for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests the bedroom, but it is a garden bed being raked.
explanation.definitionFit: A raker uses a rake to level soil when getting a flower bed ready.

clue.text: Fell for swindle

definitions.meaning: to cheat them out of money

explanation.definitionFit: A fell is an animal's hide, and to skin someone is slang for fleecing them.

clue.text: Taste defeat

definitions.meaning: a small taste, as of paint or flavour
to beat, as in we can ... them

explanation.definitionFit: A lick is a small sampling with the tongue, and to lick an opponent is to beat them.

clue.text: Plant producing heavy blooms

parts.note: reads like a flowering shrub, but the plant is a factory and blooms are thick bars of iron made there

explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is a heavy ingot of iron or steel, so the factory making them is a foundry of that metal.

clue.text: Girl going by horse, with set-end half in van

indicators.note: the end half of the word is set in the van, the front, so the back three letters move forward

parts.note: riding means travelling on horseback

explanation.surface: A girl rides out, with half the troop at the end sent up front.
explanation.walkthrough: Van means the front. Splitting RIDING as RID and ING and putting the end half first gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a girl's name of Scandinavian origin.

clue.text: Bites back, skirting round issue in final performance

indicators.note: going round the outside of something, so the other piece sits within
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: gnaws means bites
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: An actor snaps back while dodging the question in his last show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal and 'skirting round' the container: the offspring sits inside the reversed bites word, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is someone's last appearance, from the legend that swans sing just before dying.
